title: Agentic browsers - the AI that browses and acts with your credentials, and the unsolved prompt-injection hole
source: Public record: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas (macOS-first) on Oct 21 2025 - ChatGPT embedded in every page, an 'Ask ChatGPT' sidebar, and an 'Agent Mode' (preview, paid) that autonomously clicks through sites to complete multi-step tasks (research, shopping, forms), operating on sites the user is already SIGNED IN to and using 'browser memories' of prior visits; OpenAI framed it as a step toward 'a true super-assistant that understands your world' and shipped safeguards (blocks code execution, file downloads, extension installs, filesystem access) + disclosed prompt-injection risk. Perplexity launched the Comet browser Jul 9 2025 (Max, later broadened); the 2025 AI Agent Index rates Comet at L4-L5 autonomy - it proceeds autonomously once initiated, with fewer approval gates than ChatGPT Agent. SECURITY: Brave's security team (Aug 2025) showed Comet feeds webpage content to its LLM without separating the user's instructions from untrusted page content, enabling INDIRECT PROMPT INJECTION - a malicious Reddit post can instruct the agent to open the user's logged-in Gmail, trigger an account-recovery flow, and exfiltrate the code; payloads hide as white-on-white text, HTML comments, or text inside images/screenshots. These bypass same-origin policy and browser sandboxes because the agent has LEGITIMATE multi-domain access with the user's credentials. Brave concluded it is a SYSTEMIC, category-wide problem, not a single-vendor bug. LayerX disclosed 'CometJacking' (one crafted URL exfiltrates email/calendar/connected-service data); Perplexity reportedly marked reports 'no security impact / not applicable' and a Brave-reported fix was later defeated. Trail of Bits (pre-launch audit) found four prompt-injection techniques exfiltrating Gmail. HONESTY/GRADE: the product launches, dates, features, and the disclosed vulnerabilities + vendor responses are FACT (vendor posts + Brave/LayerX/Trail of Bits/Simon Willison research); the 'surveillance/control-surface' framing (an agent that sees all browsing and acts with your credentials concentrates enormous data + authority) is LABELED interpretation; no claim that any vendor misuses the data - the point is the attack surface + concentration, not asserted intent. Overlay/structural edges only; new nodes do not perturb the AI-financial SCC (unchanged). Cross-refs: spec-heif-heist-openai-ciso (prompt injection as an acknowledged frontier), the surveillance layer, spec-local-uncensored-ai (the counter-ecosystem).

edges.notes: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas (macOS-first, Oct 21 2025): ChatGPT in every page + an Agent Mode (preview, paid) that acts on SIGNED-IN sites and uses 'browser memories' - OpenAI's 'super-assistant that understands your world'. Shipped safeguards (no code exec/downloads/extensions/filesystem) + disclosed prompt-injection risk (fact).
Perplexity's Comet (launched Jul 9 2025) is rated L4-L5 autonomy (2025 AI Agent Index) - it proceeds autonomously once initiated, with fewer approval gates than ChatGPT Agent (fact).

Google is embedding Gemini agentic features into Chrome - the incumbent browser leader moving the same direction, which makes agentic browsing a mass-market default rather than a niche (fact of the direction).

The defining, UNSOLVED security hole: the agent feeds untrusted webpage content to its LLM without separating it from the user's instructions, so hidden page text (white-on-white, HTML comments, text-in-images) becomes commands. Brave (Aug 2025) demoed Comet exfiltrating a logged-in Gmail recovery code from a malicious Reddit post; LayerX's 'CometJacking' exfiltrates email/calendar via one crafted URL; Trail of Bits found four Gmail-exfil techniques pre-launch. Brave's verdict: systemic, category-wide, not a single-vendor bug (fact of the disclosures).

Prompt injection is the acknowledged-unsolved frontier even for the leaders - OpenAI disclosed the risk at Atlas launch and its CISO has publicly treated it as an open problem (cross-ref spec-heif-heist-openai-ciso). FACT of the acknowledgement; it bypasses same-origin policy + sandboxes because the agent has legitimate credentialed multi-domain access, which traditional browser security was never designed to contain.

CONTROL-SURFACE framing (labeled interpretation): an agent that sees ALL of a user's browsing and acts with their logged-in credentials across domains concentrates enormous data + authority in one AI vendor - a qualitatively new surveillance/control surface vs a passive browser. No vendor misuse is asserted; the point is the attack surface + data concentration, not intent (cross-ref the surveillance layer, digitalid-corporate).

Brave's security team is the lead discloser - it showed the architectural root cause (no trust boundary between user instructions and page content) and that attempted vendor fixes were later defeated; its recommended defense is to cleanly separate trusted user instructions from untrusted website content before sending to the model (fact; the fix is unproven at category scale).
